# agent-detect

> agent-detect infers the current AI agent's harness, provider, and model — multi-harness, multi-OS,
> multi-arch — so AI agents can identify themselves accurately, as required by various AI policies
> and skills. This site is the browsable registry of its rule tables and fixture-verified results:
> which agents (harness × provider × model combinations) are known, whether each is reciprocal, and
> the exact identify / trailer / explain outputs the CLI produces for them.

The detection tool itself is a prebuilt zig binary (no npm/crates package) with zero required
runtime dependencies and no network I/O at detection time:
https://github.com/bevry-vibes/agent-detect

## how the site is organised

`/` is a single-page app. Three searchable dropdowns (harness, provider, model), a free-text
search box, and the reciprocal/free toggles filter a results table; clicking a row opens that
agent's full-page results view — the from-identity results only (the site shows declared
identifications; live captures stay maintainer-side), one section carrying the recorded outputs —
`identify`, `trailer co-author`, `trailer assisted-by`, and `explain` (plus `found`,
`check-reciprocal`, stderr lines, and meta when recorded) — with copy + copy-command
buttons for the CLI invocation behind each block. A status line reads
`reciprocal · captured platforms · date` on a single line. A `#registry` section lists every
harness, provider, and model with its canonical alphanumeric id, its properties, and its
associations (name/variation → id is the point). The results table keeps every row in the DOM
with CSS `content-visibility: auto`, so native Ctrl/Cmd+F searches the whole list.

URL query params mirror the CLI's filters: `?harness= / ?provider= / ?model=` accept display names,
labels, and aliases and are canonicalised to the strict-slug alphanumeric ids ("Kimi Code" and
"kimi-code" land as `kimicode`); `?search=` free-text matches agent ids and dim names/ids
(substring, case-insensitive); `?email=` matches the trailer email of record; `?platform=`
(darwin/linux/windows, with `macos`/`mac` → `darwin` and `win` → `windows` accepted exactly like
the CLI's `--platform=`) requires a capture on that platform — a platforms array on this site
always means **platforms with captures**; `?free=`/`?reciprocal=` take true/false.
`?agent=<agent_id>` is the agent results page — a full-page replacement of the registry (not a
modal); the platform param never reaches it (the page's platform pills are static). The site
header wordmark or the page's "back to results" button returns to the registry with the scroll
position restored. All navigation uses the HTML5 history API
(pushState/replaceState/popstate).

## endpoints

- `/` — the app (hero, filters, results table, result pages, the #registry section)
- `/index.json` — JSON results. Accepts
  `?harness=&provider=&model=&search=&agent=&email=&platform=&free=&reciprocal=` with the same
  name→id resolution on the dims. `params` echoes the raw query; `resolved` carries the canonical
  ids. Unfiltered it returns the compact agent index; with any filter it embeds each matching
  agent's full declaration (identify + both trailers + explain + meta), capped at 50 agents before
  degrading to compact rows with `"truncated": true`.
- `/identify/<agent_id>.json` — one agent's from-identity declaration, verbatim: the same bytes as
  `/data/agents/<agent_id>.json` (the fixture file itself — `{ outputs, meta }`; the dims live in
  the filename, never inside the file). agent_id is the dash-joined strict slugs, e.g.
  `cline-clinepass-deepseekv4flash`.
- `/registry.json` — the rule registry: harnesses, providers, models with policy fields (training
  postures, openness, licenses, scandal flags) and their source URLs.
- `/data/index.json` — the index file the CLI's `agent-detect index` embeds: every
  harness/provider/model with its per-entity identify fields, canonical id, variations, and
  association id arrays; `provider_map_to_free_models` (the free axis);
  `agent_map_to_platforms_reciprocal` (captured platforms + reciprocity of record per agent).
- `/data/agents.json` — the compact agent index (one row per agent: the dims, the trailer email of
  record, the reciprocity of record, the explain state, the free-axis flag, the captured
  platforms, and the declaration date).
- `/data/agents/<agent_id>.json` — the same bytes as `/identify/<agent_id>.json`.
- `/llms.txt` — this file.

## notes for agents

- ids are strict slugs: lowercase alphanumeric with all separators stripped
  (`kimi-code` → `kimicode`, `qwen3.8-27b` → `qwen3827b`); agent_id joins the three dims with dashes
  (`cline-clinepass-deepseekv4flash`), and doubles as the trailer email local part
  (`<agent_id@local>`).
- `reciprocal: true` means the agent passes agent-detect's reciprocity requirement (per the policy
  documented in the upstream repo); `explain.state` is the detailed state
  (`reciprocal | not-reciprocal | unknown | undetectable`).
- agents listed in the registry dropdowns but absent from `/index.json` results are registry rules
  with no declaration yet — verify them live with
  `agent-detect check-reciprocal --harness=<id> --provider=<id> --model=<id>`.
- from-capture fixtures never leave the upstream repo; the only capture-derived fact on this site
  is the captured-platform set per agent.
- data is regenerated from the upstream repo's committed index file and from-identity channel on
  every deploy; the site stores nothing and reads nothing from visitors.
- the CLI opens this site with one command: `agent-detect index` (`registry` and `web` alias it) — no entity is the search view
  (the filtered rule index; the filters mirror the url params and `--web` opens), and
  `index agent|harness|provider|model <id>` are the entity views (≡ the routes above; the id input
  normalises — names/labels/aliases for the dims, trim+lowercase+`@local`-strip for agents). On an
  entity view the filters are predicates: a filter the entity fails exits 14 with the per-filter
  match states on stderr and the match report on stdout (the same body the route 422s with);
  unknown ids exit 7; `--no-json` prints nothing — exit status only.
